title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed last week's benchmark results, discussed persistent networking flakiness (VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules), planning for a runtime upgrade next week, and agreed on smoke tests and logs to collect. Action items include Redwood sending updated upgrade window, SE to run tcpdump and share traces, and customer to open firewall exceptions for 10.5.0.0/24.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-30 10:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sara, Miguel, Priya - Redwood; James, Anika, Ravi - MediScale.

[00:00] Sara Lin: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick roll call, and then we'll dive into the pilot items.
[00:08] James Park: hey, James here - sorry, juggling the daycare drop-off but I'm on.
[00:11] Miguel Ortega: miguel, se here from redwood.
[00:14] Anika Bose: anika, sec on my side.
[00:16] Priya Kaur: priya csm.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: ravi, ml eng.

[00:25] Sara Lin: cool, thanks. agenda — quick review of the benchmark sheet we shared, network troubleshooting, upgrade schedule for the runtime bump, and next steps. i posted the benchmark link in chat: /redwood-pilot-bench-2026-12 (note: link).

[01:02] James Park: on the benchmarks, we saw average p50 latency at 78ms but p95 spiking to 350ms on longer sequences, is that consistent with what you expect?
[01:10] Miguel Ortega: yeah those numbers line up with what we saw in the hosted runs; with the private pilot you get some network jitter and the initial KV cache miss does add, um, like 40-80ms. the p95 spikes usually correlate with cold cache and the particular routing path—i think some requests hit the NAT gateway and others go straight via the peered route.
[01:36] Ravi Patel: we have many model warmup requests, we tried pre-warming but there's still spike. do you recommend prefix caching?
[01:44] Miguel Ortega: absolutely, prefix/KV cache helps a lot. for your workload if you can pin certain prompt patterns we can set up a small warmup job to populate the KV cache. also the runtime upgrade includes a better cache eviction policy that should help.

[02:20] Anika Bose: can we pause, quick sec — the networking issue from last week; our infra team reported intermittent connection resets during heavy load, and we saw connection tracking exhaustion on our side.
[02:35] James Park: yeah that's been the biggest blocker; sometimes the route tables change during autoscaling and we lose the flow.
[02:42] Miguel Ortega: ok, two things to check: first, VPC peering path MTU and route propagation; second, NAT gateway connection tracking limits. we recommended using the dedicated NAT or a managed TGW route for high-throughput.
[02:58] James Park: we are on a shared NAT right now. switching to NAT-GW would cost more, any quick wins?
[03:05] Miguel Ortega: short term: increase connection tracking table, and we can route the inference nodes through a private interface to avoid the NAT for egress to internal infra. also ensure health checks are targeting the correct ENI.

[03:32] Priya Kaur: redwood will also share a packet capture pattern we want you to run — miguel?
[03:37] Miguel Ortega: yes i'll drop a tcpdump command and a filter for the inference ports; please run it during a spike and upload the .pcap to the shared folder.

[04:00] Ravi Patel: noted. i'll get ops to run that. regarding the firewall, do you need specific ports open for the control plane?
[04:08] Sara Lin: the private control plane uses 443 to our control endpoint and a few ephemeral ports for downloads; we'll send the exact CIDRs. currently we asked for 10.5.0.0/24 to be reachable from your infra for the management interface.
[04:24] Anika Bose: security question — where are the audit logs stored in the private deployment? we need to ensure they go to our KMS and are retained for 13 months.
[04:33] Miguel Ortega: by default the logs write to S3 in your account and you can point the KMS key at your CMK; we've done a config for customer-managed keys. retention is configurable — we'll include the config snippet.

[05:05] James Park: ok thanks. next, upgrade window — you mentioned a runtime upgrade to 1.12 that fixes eviction and has performance kernels for A100/80. what's the risk and expected downtime?
[05:18] Miguel Ortega: the upgrade is rolling per node, we don't expect full downtime. small per-node restart ~2-3 minutes when the model files get recompiled, and a brief period of higher latency for requests that hit a node mid-upgrade. overall we'd plan a 2-hour window to be safe for the cluster.
[05:36] Sara Lin: for production we usually do canary first — 10% of traffic to the new runtime for 30 minutes, ramp to 50, then full. for the pilot we can do a faster ramp if you want.
[05:47] Ravi Patel: can we run the upgrade against a subset of models first? we have internal critical prompts.
[05:52] Miguel Ortega: yes, we can pin model versions per route; we'll keep the old runtime variant for the critical routes during the initial canary.

[06:10] Anika Bose: also need to see the security release notes — any CVEs?
[06:15] Miguel Ortega: no customer-impacting CVEs in 1.12; we'll include the full changelog in the update email.

[06:30] James Park: are there any known regressions in output quality after the quantization changes you mentioned? we rely on high fidelity for our summaries.
[06:39] Miguel Ortega: the quantization path is opt-in for now; we did local evals and saw negligible quality drift on the models you're using, but we'll run a quick eval on your eval set as a precaution.

[07:05] Priya Kaur: action item: redwood to run eval on mediScale evalset and share results.
[07:10] Miguel Ortega: yep, i'll coordinate with ravi on the dataset location.

[07:20] Ravi Patel: i'll share the eval set link after the call.

[07:27] Sara Lin: ok id like to go over the logs we need — please capture: tcpdump during spike, inference server logs, and the health checker output. also we'll need your cloud console support logs in case the route propagations changed.

[08:00] James Park: one weird intermittent error we saw in the logs is 'kv-cache: invalid sequence token' — not sure if it's a redwood runtime thing or our proxy.
[08:09] Miguel Ortega: that message is usually from a mismatch in model version metadata during warmup; it can happen when an older process still holds a cache handle while the model files update. 1.12's cache eviction reduces that window, so it should materially reduce occurrences.

[09:00] Anika Bose: on compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and the pen test report for the control plane — can you send those to our security mailbox?
[09:08] Sara Lin: yes, Sara will send SOC2, ISO attestation, and the pen test summary. we'll redact sensitive bits but provide attestation.

[09:22] Miguel Ortega: also, for KMS integration we'll need a cross-account IAM role to allow keywrap for the service account; i'll attach the minimal policy.

[10:00] James Park: about billing — if we move from shared NAT to dedicated NAT-GW, what kind of cost bump do you see?
[10:08] Sara Lin: it depends on egress patterns; for your current pilot traffic we estimated an incremental $1.2k/month for NAT-GW plus some throughput charges. but the runtime improvements could reduce token cost by ~8% due to better batching and cache hit rate, so net ops cost might be neutral. we'll send the updated cost model.

[11:00] Ravi Patel: one more ask — can we enable per-request tracing to capture latency breakdowns? like a token-level breakdown for a sample request?
[11:10] Miguel Ortega: yes, we can enable per-request tracing for a subset of traffic; it adds a small overhead but gives you token-level timing. we'll sample 1% by default.

[11:35] Priya Kaur: scheduling — we propose the upgrade next Wednesday 2027-01-06 during your low window at 0200 UTC, can you confirm?
[11:44] James Park: that time works for us, but can we do a canary first earlier that day?
[11:49] Sara Lin: yes we can do an early canary at 1800 UTC and then full rollout at 0200. we'll send calendar invites.

[12:20] Miguel Ortega: ok circling back on network debugging — i'll share tcpdump command, and also a short script to stress the flow to reproduce the conntrack exhaustion.

[12:40] James Park: we'll run that in our staging env and get back.

[13:00] Priya Kaur: any competitor mentions — we recently ran an eval versus vertex and anthro, any notes?
[13:09] James Park: we saw similar latencies on vertex but instrumentation is better in redwood for token-level tracing, which helps.

[13:30] Sara Lin: great. to wrap up we'll send: upgrade plan, SOC2 + pen test, tcpdump command + stress script, updated cost spreadsheet, and timeline invites.

[14:00] James Park: awesome thanks all.

[14:05] Anika Bose: thanks.

[14:07] Meeting end.

Miguel Ortega: run eval on MediScale eval set and share results by 2027-01-04
